title: Booking a community course
context: A man phones a community centre to book a place on an evening course.

voiceDesign.instruct: male, middle-aged, moderate pitch, british accent

voiceNotes.tone: Friendly, efficient and professional; clear on details.

voiceDesign.instruct: female, young adult, moderate pitch, british accent

voiceNotes.tone: Relaxed and chatty; slightly unsure when giving his number.

voiceDesign.instruct: male, young adult, low pitch, australian accent

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Part 1. You will hear a man phoning a community centre to book a place on an evening course. First, you have some time to look at questions 1 to 5.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Now listen carefully and answer questions 1 to 5.

lines.speaker: joanna
lines.text: Good morning, Riverside Community Centre, Joanna speaking. How can I help?

lines.speaker: daniel
lines.text: Oh, hi there. I'm ringing about your evening courses. I saw a few are starting soon, and I'd like to book a place on one if there's still room.

lines.speaker: joanna
lines.text: Of course. Which course were you interested in?

lines.speaker: daniel
lines.text: Well, I was really hoping to do the watercolour painting class.

lines.speaker: joanna
lines.text: Ah, I'm afraid that one's completely full. We've already got a waiting list of about ten people.

lines.speaker: daniel
lines.text: Oh, that's a shame. Are there any other art courses?

lines.speaker: joanna
lines.text: There's still space on Introduction to Pottery. It's very popular with complete beginners.

lines.speaker: daniel
lines.text: Actually, that sounds great. I've always wanted to have a go at working with clay. Let's do that one.

lines.speaker: joanna
lines.text: Lovely. I'll just take a few details, then. Could I have your name, please?

lines.speaker: daniel
lines.text: Yes, it's Daniel Halloran.

lines.speaker: joanna
lines.text: And is that H-O-L-L-O-R-A-N?
lines.direction: Spell the letters one at a time.

lines.speaker: daniel
lines.text: No, it starts with H-A. So, H-A-L-L-O-R-A-N.
lines.direction: Spell the letters one at a time, slowly and clearly.

lines.speaker: joanna
lines.text: Got it, thanks. And what is the best number to contact you on?

lines.speaker: daniel
lines.text: It's my mobile. It's 07723 418950.
lines.direction: Read the number digit by digit: oh-seven-seven-two-three, four-one-eight-nine-five-oh.

lines.speaker: daniel
lines.text: Oh, hang on, no, I always get the end of it mixed up.

lines.speaker: daniel
lines.text: Let me start again. It's 07723 418590.
lines.direction: Slower and more careful than before. Digit by digit: oh-seven-seven-two-three, four-one-eight-five-nine-oh.

lines.speaker: joanna
lines.text: Thanks. Now, the pottery course runs on two different evenings. The Tuesday group still has one or two places left.

lines.speaker: daniel
lines.text: Tuesday's tricky for me, I'm afraid. I've got football training that night.

lines.speaker: joanna
lines.text: That's no problem. The other group meets on Thursday evenings, from seven till nine.

lines.speaker: daniel
lines.text: Perfect, that works much better for me.

lines.speaker: joanna
lines.text: The course was originally going to start on the 30th of October.

lines.speaker: daniel
lines.text: Oh, so that would be next week, then?

lines.speaker: joanna
lines.text: Well, no. The tutor's away that week, so the first class has been moved to the 6th of November.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Before you hear the rest of the conversation, you have some time to look at questions 6 to 10.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Now listen and answer questions 6 to 10.

lines.speaker: daniel
lines.text: So, how much does the course cost?

lines.speaker: joanna
lines.text: The full price for the ten weeks is 120 pounds.

lines.speaker: daniel
lines.text: Ouch. Is there any kind of discount?

lines.speaker: joanna
lines.text: Do you live in the borough?

lines.speaker: daniel
lines.text: Yes, I'm on Mill Lane, just round the corner from you.

lines.speaker: joanna
lines.text: Then you qualify for the residents' rate, which brings it down to 96 pounds. That includes all the clay and the firing.

lines.speaker: daniel
lines.text: Great. And do I need to buy any tools or anything?

lines.speaker: joanna
lines.text: No, the tools are all provided, and there are plenty of glazes to choose from.

lines.speaker: daniel
lines.text: What about gloves? I imagine it gets pretty messy.

lines.speaker: joanna
lines.text: We have gloves here for anyone who wants them. The only thing you need to bring yourself is an apron.

lines.speaker: daniel
lines.text: Right. And is there anywhere to park? I usually drive.

lines.speaker: joanna
lines.text: Please don't use the supermarket car park next door. They give fines after an hour.

lines.speaker: joanna
lines.text: There's a free car park behind the library, though, and it's only a two-minute walk from here.

lines.speaker: daniel
lines.text: Good to know, thanks.

lines.speaker: joanna
lines.text: Just for our records, can I ask how you heard about the course?

lines.speaker: daniel
lines.text: Hmm, I picked up one of your leaflets at the doctor's surgery a while ago, and a neighbour mentioned it too.

lines.speaker: daniel
lines.text: But what actually made me ring was an advert on the radio last week.

lines.speaker: joanna
lines.text: Thanks. And one last thing. Do you have any allergies the tutor should know about?

lines.speaker: daniel
lines.text: Nothing food-related, but I do react quite badly to latex.

lines.speaker: joanna
lines.text: OK, I'll make a note of that for the tutor. Right, you're all booked. You'll get a confirmation email later today.

lines.speaker: daniel
lines.text: Brilliant. Thanks so much for your help. Bye.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: That is the end of Part 1. You now have one minute to check your answers to Part 1.
